Amphibious UAV for Real-Time 3D Volumetric Air Pollution Monitoring

A dual-mode (aerial + ground) drone platform built around an ESP32-WROOM and an Arduino UNO linked over I2C. A PMS7003 sensor measures PM1.0, PM2.5 and PM10, and a NEO-6M GPS tags every reading with its location. An ESP32 web dashboard shows live values, logs data to CSV and feeds 2D and 3D pollution maps; an MPU6050 senses orientation and servo-driven foldable arms handle the ground-to-flight transformation.

ESP32-WROOMArduino UNOPMS7003NEO-6M GPSMPU6050I2CMotor control

Main controller (report excerpts): MPU6050 orientation, data logging to flash, web endpoint and main loop with safety checks.

drone_esp32_main.ino
// Amphibian Drone - ESP32-WROOM main controller (selected excerpts)
//
// Source: report Section 5.4.5 - 5.4.9. The full firmware also contains the
// Wi-Fi / web-server routes, servo + ESC control, GPS filtering and the flight
// sequence; those helper functions and globals are defined elsewhere, so this
// file shows the main program structure rather than a standalone sketch.

// ---------- System initialization (5.4.5) ----------
void setup() {
  GPSserial.begin(9600, SERIAL_8N1, 16, 17);   // GPS on GPIO16 / GPIO17
  LittleFS.begin(true);                        // flash file system for logs
  Wire.begin(I2C_SDA, I2C_SCL);                // I2C master -> Arduino UNO
  Wire.setClock(100000);
  // Initialize the dedicated MPU6050 I2C bus (GPIO4 SDA, GPIO13 SCL).
  // Initialize the MPU6050 sensor.
  // Initialize servos and ESCs.
  // Configure Wi-Fi and web-server routes.
  // Initialize the system clock.
  // Ensure the motors remain stopped at startup.
}

// ---------- MPU6050 orientation (complementary filter, 5.4.6) ----------
void updateMpu6050() {
  if (!imuReady || millis() - imuLastReadMillis < IMU_INTERVAL_MS) return;
  imuLastReadMillis = millis();

  uint8_t b[14];
  if (!mpuReadBytes(0x3B, b, 14)) {
    imuReady = false;
    return;
  }
  int16_t ax = (b[0] << 8) | b[1];
  int16_t ay = (b[2] << 8) | b[3];
  int16_t az = (b[4] << 8) | b[5];
  int16_t gx = (b[8] << 8) | b[9];
  int16_t gy = (b[10] << 8) | b[11];
  int16_t gz = (b[12] << 8) | b[13];

  float dt = (micros() - imuLastMicros) / 1e6f;
  imuLastMicros = micros();
  if (dt <= 0 || dt > 0.1f) dt = 0.01f;

  imuGyroX = gx / 131.0f - imuGyroBiasX;
  imuGyroY = gy / 131.0f - imuGyroBiasY;
  imuGyroZ = gz / 131.0f - imuGyroBiasZ;

  float accRoll  = atan2(ay, sqrt(ax * ax + az * az)) * 180 / PI;
  float accPitch = atan2(-ax, sqrt(ay * ay + az * az)) * 180 / PI;

  imuRoll  = 0.98f * (imuRoll  + imuGyroX * dt) + 0.02f * accRoll;
  imuPitch = 0.98f * (imuPitch + imuGyroY * dt) + 0.02f * accPitch;
  imuYaw  += imuGyroZ * dt;
}

// ---------- Web endpoint for pollution data (5.4.7) ----------
// Route registration pattern:
server.on("/pms-data", handlePmsData);

// ---------- Pollution + GPS data logging to LittleFS as CSV (5.4.8) ----------
void appendPmsGpsLog(uint16_t pm1, uint16_t pm25, uint16_t pm10) {
  if (!fsReady || pmsLogFull) return;
  if (LittleFS.totalBytes() - LittleFS.usedBytes() < PMS_LOG_MIN_FREE_BYTES) {
    pmsLogFull = true;
    return;
  }
  File f = LittleFS.open(PMS_LOG_FILE, FILE_APPEND);
  if (!f) return;

  char ts[24] = "";
  struct tm t;
  if (getLocalTime(&t, 0))
    strftime(ts, sizeof(ts), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", &t);

  const unsigned long now = millis();
  const bool quality  = gpsQualityGood();
  const bool filtered = quality && gpsHistoryCount > 0 &&
                        (now - gpsLastAcceptedMs < GPS_FIX_MAX_AGE_MS);

  f.printf("%s,%lu,%u,%u,%u,%s,", ts, now, pm1, pm25, pm10,
           filtered ? "GOOD" : "INVALID");
  if (filtered) {
    f.print(gps.location.lat(), 7); f.print(',');
    f.print(gps.location.lng(), 7); f.print(',');
    f.print(gpsFilteredLat, 7);     f.print(',');
    f.print(gpsFilteredLon, 7);
  }
  f.close();
}

// ---------- Main execution loop (5.4.9) ----------
void loop() {
  updateMpu6050();
  readGps();
  server.handleClient();
  readGps();

  // Request pollution data from the UNO once per second
  if (millis() - lastPmsReadMillis >= PMS_READ_INTERVAL_MS) {
    lastPmsReadMillis = millis();
    readPmsDataFromUno();

    if (pmsDataValid)
      appendPmsGpsLog(pmsPM1, pmsPM25, pmsPM10);
  }

  // Update flight sequence and IMU control
  updateFlightSequence();
  applyImuFlightControl();

  // Safety checks
  if (WiFi.status() != WL_CONNECTED) {
    if (systemStarted) {
      sendMotorCommand('S', 0);
      resetFlightMode();
      systemStarted = false;
    }
  } else if (systemStarted &&
             (millis() - lastCommandMillis > COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS)) {
    sendMotorCommand('S', 0);
    resetFlightMode();
    systemStarted = false;
  }
}

UNO node: reads the PMS7003 sensor, answers the ESP32 over I2C (address 0x08) and drives the ground motors.

drone_uno_node.ino
// Amphibian Drone - Arduino UNO node
// Reads the PMS7003 particulate sensor and drives the two ground motors
// through an L293D. Acts as I2C SLAVE (address 0x08) for the ESP32 master.
//
// Source: excerpts from the project report (Section 5.4.1 - 5.4.4).
// Parts marked [glue] were added to make the sketch complete and compile.

#include <Wire.h>
#include <SoftwareSerial.h>

#define I2C_ADDRESS 0x08

// L293D pin assignment used in the project
#define ENA 5
#define ENB 6
#define IN1 7
#define IN2 8
#define IN3 9
#define IN4 10

SoftwareSerial pmsSerial(2, 3);          // PMS7003: RX = D2, TX = D3, 9600 baud

uint16_t pm1_0 = 0, pm2_5 = 0, pm10 = 0;
uint8_t  buffer[32];
volatile char    motorCmd   = 'S';       // [glue] last command from the ESP32
volatile uint8_t motorSpeed = 0;         // [glue] PWM 0-255

void setup() {
  Wire.begin(I2C_ADDRESS);
  Wire.onReceive(receiveEvent);
  Wire.onRequest(requestEvent);
  pmsSerial.begin(9600);
  pinMode(5, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(6, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(7, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(8, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(9, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(10, OUTPUT);
  stopMotors();
}

void loop() {
  readPms();                             // [glue]
  driveMotors(motorCmd, motorSpeed);     // [glue]
}

// ---- PMS7003 data frame validation (report 5.4.2) ----
void readPms() {                         // [glue] collects one 32-byte frame
  while (pmsSerial.available() >= 32) {
    if (pmsSerial.peek() != 0x42) { pmsSerial.read(); continue; }
    for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++) buffer[i] = pmsSerial.read();

    if (buffer[0] == 0x42 && buffer[1] == 0x4D) {
      uint16_t checksum = 0;
      for (int i = 0; i < 30; i++) {
        checksum += buffer[i];
      }
      uint16_t receivedChecksum = ((uint16_t)buffer[30] << 8) | buffer[31];
      if (checksum == receivedChecksum) {
        pm1_0 = ((uint16_t)buffer[10] << 8) | buffer[11];
        pm2_5 = ((uint16_t)buffer[12] << 8) | buffer[13];
        pm10  = ((uint16_t)buffer[14] << 8) | buffer[15];
      }
    }
  }
}

// ---- Sending pollution data through I2C (report 5.4.3) ----
// Six bytes, big-endian: PM1.0, PM2.5, PM10
void requestEvent() {
  Wire.write(highByte(pm1_0));
  Wire.write(lowByte(pm1_0));
  Wire.write(highByte(pm2_5));
  Wire.write(lowByte(pm2_5));
  Wire.write(highByte(pm10));
  Wire.write(lowByte(pm10));
}

// [glue] ESP32 sends: command character ('F','B','L','R','S') + speed byte
void receiveEvent(int howMany) {
  if (Wire.available()) motorCmd = (char)Wire.read();
  if (Wire.available()) motorSpeed = Wire.read();
  while (Wire.available()) Wire.read();
}

// ---- Ground motor control (report 5.4.4) ----
void driveMotors(char cmd, uint8_t speed) {
  analogWrite(ENA, speed);
  analogWrite(ENB, speed);
  if (cmd == 'F') {                      // both motors forward
    digitalWrite(IN1, HIGH); digitalWrite(IN2, LOW);
    digitalWrite(IN3, HIGH); digitalWrite(IN4, LOW);
  } else if (cmd == 'B') {               // both motors backward
    digitalWrite(IN1, LOW);  digitalWrite(IN2, HIGH);
    digitalWrite(IN3, LOW);  digitalWrite(IN4, HIGH);
  } else if (cmd == 'L') {               // opposite directions: turn left
    digitalWrite(IN1, LOW);  digitalWrite(IN2, HIGH);
    digitalWrite(IN3, HIGH); digitalWrite(IN4, LOW);
  } else if (cmd == 'R') {               // opposite directions: turn right
    digitalWrite(IN1, HIGH); digitalWrite(IN2, LOW);
    digitalWrite(IN3, LOW);  digitalWrite(IN4, HIGH);
  } else {                               // 'S' = stop
    stopMotors();
  }
}

void stopMotors() {
  analogWrite(ENA, 0);
  analogWrite(ENB, 0);
  digitalWrite(IN1, LOW); digitalWrite(IN2, LOW);
  digitalWrite(IN3, LOW); digitalWrite(IN4, LOW);
}
  1. The ESP32-WROOM is the main controller: it runs the web dashboard, reads the MPU6050 and GPS, and acts as I2C master.
  2. The Arduino UNO is the I2C slave (0x08): it reads the PMS7003 over UART and drives the two N20 geared motors through an L293D.
  3. Every second the ESP32 requests six bytes (PM1.0, PM2.5, PM10) from the UNO and logs valid readings with GPS to flash (CSV).
  4. Four SG90 servos fold the rotor arms: 0° folded for ground mode, about 109° deployed for flight.
  5. If Wi-Fi drops or no command arrives within the timeout, the motors stop and flight mode resets.
  6. Logged data is used to generate the 2D and 3D volumetric pollution maps.

Embedded Fire Detection & Alert System

An 8051-based embedded system for early fire and smoke hazard detection. An MQ2 gas sensor is monitored in real time, and interrupt-driven buzzer and LED alert logic written in Embedded C gives a low-latency emergency response. The full circuit and a custom PCB layout were designed and simulated in Proteus and EasyEDA.

8051 / AT89S52Embedded CMQ2 gas sensorInterruptsProteusEasyEDAPCB design

Embedded C (Keil C51): sensor output triggers the INT0 interrupt, which raises the LED and buzzer alert.

fire_8051.c
/*
 * Embedded Fire Detection & Alert System - AT89S52 (8051), Keil C51
 * MQ2 gas/smoke sensor module (digital output) -> external interrupt INT0
 *
 *   MQ2 DO  -> P3.2 (INT0)   output goes LOW when gas/smoke exceeds the threshold
 *   LED     -> P1.0          (through a series resistor)
 *   Buzzer  -> P1.4
 *   Clock   : 11.0592 MHz crystal, supply: 5 V from a 7805 regulator
 */
#include <reg52.h>

sbit MQ2_DO = P3^2;
sbit LED    = P1^0;
sbit BUZZER = P1^4;

volatile bit alarm = 0;                 // set by the interrupt, cleared in main

void delay_ms(unsigned int ms) {        // approx. delay at 11.0592 MHz
    unsigned int i, j;
    for (i = 0; i < ms; i++)
        for (j = 0; j < 123; j++);
}

/* INT0 interrupt service routine: runs the moment the sensor output falls */
void ext0_isr(void) interrupt 0 {
    alarm = 1;
}

void main(void) {
    LED = 0;
    BUZZER = 0;

    MQ2_DO = 1;                         // release pin so it can be used as input
    IT0 = 1;                            // INT0 triggers on falling edge
    EX0 = 1;                            // enable external interrupt 0
    EA  = 1;                            // global interrupt enable

    while (1) {
        if (alarm) {                    // fire / smoke hazard detected
            LED = 1;
            BUZZER = 1;  delay_ms(200); // pulsing alarm tone
            BUZZER = 0;  delay_ms(200);

            if (MQ2_DO == 1) {          // reading back to normal -> reset alarm
                alarm = 0;
                LED = 0;
                BUZZER = 0;
            }
        }
    }
}
  1. The MQ2 sensor module’s digital output is wired to the 8051’s INT0 pin (P3.2).
  2. When gas or smoke crosses the threshold, the output falls and the interrupt service routine fires immediately, giving low-latency response.
  3. The main loop then drives the LED and a pulsing buzzer until the reading returns to normal.
  4. Power: 9 V input regulated to 5 V by a 7805 (0.1 µF in, 10 µF out). Clock: 11.0592 MHz crystal with two 33 pF capacitors. Reset: 10 kΩ + 10 µF network.
  5. The circuit was simulated in Proteus, tested on a breadboard, then laid out as a custom PCB in EasyEDA.

Automated License Plate Recognition System for Smart Parking

A computer-vision vehicle identification pipeline on a Raspberry Pi. OpenCV handles real-time image capture and preprocessing, an OCR-based algorithm detects and reads the number plate with improved accuracy under variable lighting, and a relational database automates entry/exit logging and access control.

PythonOpenCVTesseract OCRRaspberry PiSQL databaseGPIO
GitHub ↗

Raspberry Pi code: plate detection, OCR, database logging and gate control.

lpr_parking.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
License Plate Recognition (LPR) Parking System - Raspberry Pi
Camera -> OpenCV plate detection -> Tesseract OCR -> SQLite log -> servo gate

Install (Raspberry Pi OS):
    sudo apt install tesseract-ocr python3-opencv python3-gpiozero
    pip install pytesseract
"""
import re
import sqlite3
import time
from collections import deque
from datetime import datetime

import cv2
import pytesseract
from gpiozero import AngularServo, LED

# ---------------- Configuration ----------------
CAMERA_INDEX = 0
SERVO_PIN = 18            # gate servo signal (BCM numbering)
LED_GREEN, LED_RED = 23, 24
DB_FILE = "parking.db"
PLATE_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Z]{2}\d{2}[A-Z]{1,3}\d{4}$")   # e.g. MH46AB1234
CONFIRM_READS = 3         # same plate must be read N times in a row
GATE_OPEN_SECONDS = 5

gate = AngularServo(SERVO_PIN, min_angle=0, max_angle=90, initial_angle=0)
green, red = LED(LED_GREEN), LED(LED_RED)


# ---------------- Database ----------------
def init_db():
    db = sqlite3.connect(DB_FILE)
    db.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS vehicles(plate TEXT PRIMARY KEY, owner TEXT)")
    db.execute("""CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS log(
                    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                    plate TEXT, entry_time TEXT, exit_time TEXT)""")
    db.commit()
    return db


def is_authorized(db, plate):
    return db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM vehicles WHERE plate=?", (plate,)).fetchone() is not None


def log_event(db, plate):
    """Toggle: no open record -> log ENTRY, open record -> log EXIT."""
    now = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    row = db.execute("SELECT id FROM log WHERE plate=? AND exit_time IS NULL", (plate,)).fetchone()
    if row:
        db.execute("UPDATE log SET exit_time=? WHERE id=?", (now, row[0]))
        event = "EXIT"
    else:
        db.execute("INSERT INTO log(plate, entry_time) VALUES(?,?)", (plate, now))
        event = "ENTRY"
    db.commit()
    return event


# ---------------- Image processing ----------------
def find_plate(frame):
    """Return a cropped, thresholded plate image, or None."""
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    gray = cv2.bilateralFilter(gray, 11, 17, 17)        # remove noise, keep edges
    edges = cv2.Canny(gray, 30, 200)
    contours, _ = cv2.findContours(edges, cv2.RETR_TREE, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
    contours = sorted(contours, key=cv2.contourArea, reverse=True)[:10]

    for c in contours:
        approx = cv2.approxPolyDP(c, 0.018 * cv2.arcLength(c, True), True)
        if len(approx) != 4:
            continue
        x, y, w, h = cv2.boundingRect(approx)
        if h == 0 or not (2.0 < w / h < 6.0) or w < 80:  # plate-like aspect ratio
            continue
        plate = gray[y:y + h, x:x + w]
        plate = cv2.resize(plate, None, fx=2, fy=2, interpolation=cv2.INTER_CUBIC)
        _, plate = cv2.threshold(plate, 0, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY + cv2.THRESH_OTSU)
        return plate
    return None


def read_plate(plate_img):
    config = "--psm 7 -c tessedit_char_whitelist=ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789"
    text = pytesseract.image_to_string(plate_img, config=config)
    text = re.sub(r"[^A-Z0-9]", "", text.upper())
    return text if PLATE_RE.match(text) else None


# ---------------- Gate control ----------------
def open_gate():
    green.on()
    gate.angle = 90
    time.sleep(GATE_OPEN_SECONDS)
    gate.angle = 0
    green.off()


def deny():
    for _ in range(3):
        red.on(); time.sleep(0.2); red.off(); time.sleep(0.2)


# ---------------- Main loop ----------------
def main():
    db = init_db()
    cam = cv2.VideoCapture(CAMERA_INDEX)
    recent = deque(maxlen=CONFIRM_READS)
    last_plate, last_time = None, 0
    print("LPR system running. Press Ctrl+C to stop.")

    try:
        while True:
            ok, frame = cam.read()
            if not ok:
                continue

            plate_img = find_plate(frame)
            plate = read_plate(plate_img) if plate_img is not None else None
            recent.append(plate)

            # act only when the same valid plate is read several times in a row
            if plate and len(recent) == CONFIRM_READS and len(set(recent)) == 1:
                if plate != last_plate or time.time() - last_time > 30:
                    if is_authorized(db, plate):
                        event = log_event(db, plate)
                        print(f"{plate}: {event} - gate opening")
                        open_gate()
                    else:
                        print(f"{plate}: not registered - access denied")
                        deny()
                    last_plate, last_time = plate, time.time()
                    recent.clear()
            time.sleep(0.1)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        cam.release()
        gate.angle = 0
        db.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
  1. The camera captures a frame; OpenCV converts it to greyscale, filters noise and finds edges.
  2. A four-corner contour with a plate-like aspect ratio is cropped and thresholded.
  3. Tesseract reads the characters; the text is checked against the Indian plate format.
  4. The same plate must be read three times in a row before any action is taken.
  5. The SQL database is checked: registered vehicles are logged as ENTRY or EXIT and the servo opens the gate; unknown plates flash the red LED.
